query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: The introduction of coherent precipitates through aging processes can increase the coercive field of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Aging process to introduce coherent precipitates
generation.conditions: Aging temperature and time to be optimized for precipitate formation
generation.mechanism: Precipitation hardening and potential pinning of domain walls
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi with low coercive field (<100 Oe)
generation.boundary: Aging conditions (temperature, time) and composition of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: Optimal aging conditions and precipitate characteristics for maximum coercive field enhancement

falsification_experiment.design: Aging treatment of single-phase fcc FeCoNi high-entropy alloy samples at varying temperatures and times, followed by magnetic property measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no significant increase in coercive field is observed with the introduction of coherent precipitates, the hypothesis is falsified
